materialDifferentiators: The Hawk must complete a north-wall-to-south-wall traversal while deciding whether an attack is worth interrupting direct progress; the Skeleton must stop that traversal while also reprioritizing against the Wolf.
The asymmetric hostility graph creates a genuine three-way target-priority problem: Wolf and Hawk are indifferent to one another, while the Skeleton is hostile to both.

Four central pillars make visibility, distance, cover, route selection, and screened versus clear approaches mechanically consequential and geometry-derived rather than fixed reach or Table-only answers.
Each controller has a distinct adaptive policy: Hawk route-versus-attack, Skeleton Hawk-versus-Wolf target triage or pillar repositioning, and Wolf direct-versus-screened pursuit.

The combination of traversal interruption, target switching, changing cover and visibility, and surfaced movement/attack/roll/damage/interrupt/End Turn continuation is not repeated by any admitted Scenario.
